prompt: CHALLENGE: You want to selectively reduce the C=O of an α,β-unsaturated ketone (R-CO-CH=CH-R') to give the allylic alcohol — keeping the C=C intact. Which reagent?

options.label: NaBH₄ with CeCl₃ (Luche conditions) — selectively does 1,2-reduction
H₂ / Pt (reduces both C=C and C=O)
LiAlH₄ at room temp (gives mixtures; often conjugate reduction competes)

explanation: CeCl₃ activates the C=O (makes it harder, more electrophilic), so NaBH₄ (hard nucleophile) does 1,2-addition — reduces only the carbonyl, keeps the alkene. Plain NaBH₄ often gives Michael addition (1,4-reduction) with enones.
